root_cause.text: An off-by-one error in the loop bounds check within the `init_card` function of the ALSA caiaq driver allows copying up to 16 non-space characters into a 16-byte local buffer, leaving no room for a null terminator and leading to a stack out-of-bounds read when the string is processed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the loop condition in `sound/usb/caiaq/device.c` being changed from `len < sizeof(card->id)` to `len < sizeof(card->id) - 1` to ensure a null terminator is preserved in the local `id` buffer.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerable code in the `init_card` function. Specifically, the loop `for (c = card->shortname, len = 0; *c && len < sizeof(card->id); c++)` allows `len` to reach `sizeof(card->id)` (which is 16). If 16 non-space characters are copied, all 16 bytes of the `id` buffer are filled, overwriting the null terminator. When `snd_card_set_id(card, id)` is subsequently called, it processes `id` as a null-terminated string, leading to an out-of-bounds read on the stack.
